extracted.intended_audience: small businesses and small business concerns seeking to do research/receive SBIR/STTR or other DARPA funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for small businesses on engaging with DARPA: characteristics of DARPA BAAs, distinctions among solicitation types (seedlings, challenges, programs, SBIR/STTR), topic release and submission process, and the DARPA Transition and Commercialization Support Program (TCSP).

rubrics_metrics.name: BAA Characteristics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No common Statement of Work (SOW); varying technical approaches/solutions are anticipated; proposals are evaluated with technical quality and approach as the main factor; communication with proposers allowed during the open period of the BAA; consider the Heilmeier questions when communicating with DARPA; white papers or proposal abstracts may be solicited; usually have Industry Days where Program Managers brief interested communities on the research program solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Heilmeier Catechism
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the Heilmeier questions when communicating with DARPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DARPA suggests proposers and program discussions be informed by the Heilmeier catechism (link provided). Use these questions to frame technical rationale, objectives, metrics for success, and impact when interacting with DARPA staff or preparing proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Office BAAs (program-specific and rolling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tech Offices will issue program-specific BAAs throughout the year and may also issue one or two year-long BAAs with a more general scope (rolling submission process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for both targeted, program-specific solicitations and year-long/rolling BAAs from Technical Offices; rolling BAAs allow submissions on an ongoing basis and may have broader scopes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Emphasis: Technical Quality and Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated with technical quality and approach as the main factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DARPA places primary weight on the soundness, novelty, and feasibility of the proposed technical approach when reviewing proposals; structure proposals to clearly communicate technical merit and approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication During BAA Open Period
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication with proposers allowed during the open period of the BAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers may engage with Program Managers and staff while the BAA is open—use allowed communications (e.g., Industry Days, Q&A) to clarify solicitation intent and align proposals to DARPA priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Papers / Proposal Abstracts May Be Solicited
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers or proposal abstracts may be solicited by DARPA under BAAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare concise white papers/abstracts summarizing the concept and technical approach in case the solicitation requests them; use these to get feedback or screening before full proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry Days and Program Briefings
rubrics_metrics.description: Usually have Industry Days where Program Managers brief interested communities on the research program solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend Industry Days to learn program priorities, ask questions, and network with potential partners; information presented can inform proposal framing and teaming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seedlings: scope and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Seedlings are open to all capable sources, usually submitted through Office-Wide BAA, small short duration (6-9 months) projects intended to move concepts from 'disbelief' to 'mere doubt' and may lead to next-generation program ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seedlings are short, risk-reducing efforts to test feasibility and novel ideas; proposals should focus on achieving rapid, demonstrable evidence to advance a concept's credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges: structure and prizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenges compete on unique DARPA R&D problems, tend to include phases with culminating events where winners win monetary or other prizes, and may result in prizes with up to $10M in fair market value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges are competition-based solicitations; proposals and participation should target the specific problem statement and milestone/events schedule; potential prize values can be substantial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs: multi-year, multi-disciplinary development
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs are open to all capable sources, solicited through specific program BAAs, often multi-year, multi-disciplinary efforts to develop technology to move from 'possibility' to 'capability'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program proposals should plan for longer-term execution, integration across disciplines, and clear pathways from research to demonstrated capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Eligibility and Submission Pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR solicitations are open to eligible small business concerns and are submitted through an open DoD SBIR/STTR BAA via the DoD SBIR/STTR Information Portal (https://www.dodsbirsttr.mil).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure small business eligibility requirements are met before applying; follow DoD SBIR/STTR portal submission procedures and any DARPA-specific topic instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Phase I and Phase II Funding Levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase I feasibility up to $275K; Phase II prototype development up to $1.8M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget proposals should align with the indicated phase funding caps and the scope appropriate to Phase I (feasibility) versus Phase II (prototype development).

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Program Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Congressional purposes: stimulate technological innovation; foster and encourage participation by socially and economically disadvantaged SBCs and SBCs 51% owned and controlled by women; increase private sector commercialization of Federal R&D to increase competition, productivity, and economic growth; stimulate partnership of ideas and technologies between innovative SBCs and research institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and company practices that support commercialization potential, partnership with research institutions, and inclusion goals align with program objectives and can strengthen the case for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: BAA and Topic Release Process
rubrics_metrics.description: DARPA advertises SBIR/STTR topics through the DoD year-long BAA posted to the DoD SBIR/STTR Information Portal (DSIP); DARPA SBPO releases SBIR/STTR topics on a Just-in-Time basis as they are approved; proposals are submitted to the DoD portal; see the BAA for submission specifics and templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor the DSIP for DARPA topics, follow Just-in-Time topic releases, and use BAA-provided templates and instructions for compliant submissions. Align proposals to DARPA’s primary technology programs to gain integration benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with DARPA Programs and Embedded Entrepreneurship Initiative (EEI)
rubrics_metrics.description: DARPA aligns SBIR/STTR funding opportunities with its primary technology programs to avail small businesses the benefits of integration into established program communities and may place select SBIR/STTR awardees into the DARPA Embedded Entrepreneurship Initiative (EEI) for additional commercialization assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target topics that are clearly aligned to DARPA technical programs to increase chances of integration and additional support; highlight transition/commercialization plans that make the company a candidate for EEI.

rubrics_metrics.name: TCSP Principles: Educate, Communicate, Connect
rubrics_metrics.description: The TCSP is guided by three principles: EDUCATE (teach business strategies critical to transition and commercialization), COMMUNICATE (iterate a quad chart with each SBC, obtain public release approval, use the quad to communicate technology; send weekly email alerts on opportunities), and CONNECT (coordinate portfolio reviews, TIMs, match-making activities, outreach, and one-on-one meetings with agencies, primes, and stakeholders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TCSP resources to plan beyond Phase II, create and iterate a quad chart for outreach, subscribe to TCSP communications, and engage in TCSP-facilitated matchmaking and portfolio review activities to maximize transition opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quad Chart as Main Communication Tool
rubrics_metrics.description: The quad chart is the main tool used by TCSP to communicate an SBC's technology to potential stakeholders and solicit interest in more in-depth discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a clear, concise quad chart (problem, solution/approach, milestones/metrics, transition/commercialization path) and pursue DARPA public release approval for dissemination to stakeholders.
